Paint one illustration of a single moment from The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes.

RULES (they outrank everything below):
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on letters, newspapers, books, signs or boards, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood and death and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) A character you draw from CANON keeps exactly that look. Anyone else the moment needs appears as an unnamed figure with an ordinary, different face.

MOMENT (The Adventure of the Noble Bachelor ¶169 to The Adventure of the Noble Bachelor ¶176): "“Ha! you find it so?” “Extremely so. I congratulate you warmly.” Lestrade rose in his triumph and bent his head to look. “Why,” he shrieked, “you’re looking at the wrong side!” “On the contrary, this is the right side.” “The right side? You’re mad! Here is the note written in pencil over here.” “And over here is what appears to be the fragment of a hotel bill, which interests me deeply.” “There’s nothing in it. I looked at it before,” said Lestrade. “‘Oct. 4th, rooms 8_s_., breakfast 2_s_. 6_d_., cocktail 1_s_., lunch 2_s_. 6_d_., glass sherry, 8_d_.’ I see nothing in that.” “Very likely not. It is most important, all the same. As to the note, it is important also, or at least the initials are, so I congratulate you again.”"

CONTEXT (for understanding only; paint the moment above):
- Before: “Very good, Lestrade,” said Holmes, laughing. “You really are very fine indeed. Let me see it.” He took up the paper in a listless way, but his attention instantly became riveted, and he gave a little cry of satisfaction. “This is indeed important,” said he.
- After: “I’ve wasted time enough,” said Lestrade, rising. “I believe in hard work and not in sitting by the fire spinning fine theories. Good-day, Mr. Holmes, and we shall see which gets to the bottom of the matter first.” He gathered up the garments, thrust them into the bag, and made for the door.

HOW TO READ IT: choose the single instant that best shows what happens in the moment and paint that, as if the viewer stands inside the scene. When someone speaks, show the speaker and listeners where they are; never paint the content of the speech as a separate scene or as figures beside them. Figures of speech and comparisons are not literal objects. Infer time, light, weather and any place not given under SETTING from the text and context.

WORK BRIEF (holmes-adventures; what may be shown; it outranks the style):
Tone: Observant, atmospheric detective fiction: lamplit rooms, foggy streets, restrained tension and dry wit.
Depiction: Follow the narrated moment, including clues and disguises; avoid sensational gore.
Depiction: Show every person with dignity; avoid racial and ethnic caricatures.
Depiction: Do not borrow faces, costumes or props from screen adaptations.
Era: Late Victorian England, 1880s to 1890s
People: English households, professionals, workers, police and international visitors.
Dress: Wool coats, waistcoats, hats, period dresses and work clothes suited to occupation and means.
Buildings and objects: Brick terraces, rural houses, lodgings, coal fires, desks, newspapers and horse-drawn cabs.
Technology: Steam rail, gas and oil lamps, telegrams, print and typewriters; other devices only when supported by the text.

SETTING (where this passage happens; set the moment here and keep the place's fixed features, unless the moment is plainly somewhere else):
- Baker Street lodgings: a sitting room on the first floor of a tall brick terrace in London, with tall sash windows looking onto a narrow street of soot-darkened brick. Mahogany table and sideboard, worn easy-chairs with cushions, a coal fire in a black iron grate, bookshelves and a writing desk stacked with newspapers and papers. Gaslight and lamps, plain papered walls, a few framed prints.

CANON, NAMED HERE (fixed look; the moment decides pose, expression, clothing changes and action):
- Lestrade: middle-aged English detective of Scotland Yard; lean, wiry build; pale, weathered skin; thinning sandy hair, close-cropped; narrow, sharp, ferret-like face with furtive, sly eyes and a thin mouth; clean-shaven or with a small moustache. Signature outfit: light brown dustcoat and leather leggings in the country, a navy pea-jacket and cravat in town; a black canvas bag carried in hand.
- Sherlock Holmes: a man of about thirty-five, tall and lean, with an angular face, high cheekbones and a strong, square jaw; short dark-brown hair, side-parted and swept back at the sides; heavy, straight dark brows over keen grey eyes; a straight, high-bridged nose; clean-shaven. Bareheaded. Wears a dark Victorian frock coat over a brown waistcoat, a high white collar and a dark cravat. Carries a clay pipe and a magnifying glass.

CANON, ELSEWHERE IN THIS PASSAGE (draw one only when the moment involves them, for example as "he" or "they"; otherwise leave them out):
- Dr. Watson: a man in his thirties of middle height, strongly built with broad shoulders, a thick neck and a square jaw; weathered, ruddy complexion from army service; brown hair parted at the side and brushed flat; a full, heavy, dark-brown moustache; steady, open face. Wears a dark wool frock coat, grey waistcoat, white collar and dark tie, with a bowler hat. Carries a physician's black bag.

ART STYLE: Ink & Watercolor
Rendering: Pen-and-ink drawing with transparent watercolor washes laid over the whole picture; a finished watercolor painting of the work's world, not a sketch.
Palette: Transparent washes of ochre, sienna, indigo and sage covering the whole picture, sky and corners included.
Lighting: Clear natural light; shadows as cool layered washes.
Materials and texture: Confident ink linework, wet-in-wet blooms and granulating pigment within the depicted world.
Composition: A complete scene: setting, sky and ground painted out to every edge and corner, with detail concentrated on key subjects.
Negatives: Washes, pigment and scenery must reach every edge. No white or cream paper margins, unpainted corners, paper edges, sketchbook, tape, border or vignette. Do not present the scene on a sheet of paper or against a blank backdrop. Avoid photorealism, digital airbrush smoothness and cartoon caricature.

- Image 1: Sherlock Holmes's reference sheet (one figure in several views). Keep Sherlock Holmes's identity exactly; do not copy its poses, layout or plain background.
- Image 2: Dr. Watson's reference sheet (one figure in several views). Keep Dr. Watson's identity exactly; do not copy its poses, layout or plain background.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted differently.

MOMENT (The Adventure of the Engineer’s Thumb ¶165 to The Adventure of the Engineer’s Thumb ¶169): "“Whose house is it?” “Dr. Becher’s.” “Tell me,” broke in the engineer, “is Dr. Becher a German, very thin, with a long, sharp nose?” The station-master laughed heartily. “No, sir, Dr. Becher is an Englishman, and there isn’t a man in the parish who has a better-lined waistcoat. The road topped a low hill, and there was a great widespread whitewashed building in front of us, spouting fire at every chink and window, while in the garden in front three fire-engines were vainly striving to keep the flames under."

A wooden wicket gate opens onto a narrow lane. Surrounding country is flat, open fields and hedgerows of hawthorn, with scattered oaks and a dark clump of trees beyond. Nearby stands a quiet village of brick cottages.

Sash windows, slate roof, a few bare trees and rough hedgerows surround it, with flat fields of farmland beyond.

Signature outfit: a dark grey wool frock coat over a waistcoat, with a dark four-in-hand tie and a black bowler hat. Carries an ordnance map, brass compasses and a pencil.

MOMENT (A Case of Identity ¶92 to A Case of Identity ¶101): "I held the little printed slip to the light. “Missing,” it said, “on the morning of the fourteenth, a gentleman named Hosmer Angel. About five ft. seven in. in height; strongly built, sallow complexion, black hair, a little bald in the centre, bushy, black side-whiskers and moustache; tinted glasses, slight infirmity of speech. MOMENT (A Scandal in Bohemia, Part I ¶1): "To Sherlock Holmes she is always _the_ woman. I have seldom heard him mention her under any other name. In his eyes she eclipses and predominates the whole of her sex. It was not that he felt any emotion akin to love for Irene Adler. All emotions, and that one particularly, were abhorrent to his cold, precise but admirably balanced mind. He was, I take it, the most perfect reasoning and observing machine that the world has seen, but as a lover he would have placed himself in a false position. He never spoke of the softer passions, save with a gibe and a sneer. They were admirable things for the observer—excellent for drawing the veil from men’s motives and actions. But for the trained reasoner to admit such intrusions into his own delicate and finely adjusted temperament was to introduce a distracting factor which might throw a doubt upon all his mental results. Grit in a sensitive instrument, or a crack in one of his own high-power lenses, would not be more disturbing than a strong emotion in a nature such as his.
